{{Short description|German mathematician}}
'''Ludwig Adolf{{efn|also written "Adolph"}} Sohncke''' (20 June 1807 in [[Königsberg]] (now Kaliningrad), [[Kingdom of Prussia]] – 16 January 1853 in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]], Kingdom of Prussia) was a German mathematician. He was father of the mathematician [[Leonhard Sohncke]].

==Life and work==
Ludwig Adolf Sohncke studied at the [[University of Königsberg|Albertina University]] in his native town Königsberg, was doctoral student of [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]].{{sfn|Olesko|1991|p=108}} There he began his scientific career as a private [[lecturer]] in 1833. Together with Jacobi and [[Franz Ernst Neumann]], he was co-founder and co-director of the Königsberg Seminar of Physics that aimed to install a more intensive and effective model for teaching Physics and mathematics.{{sfn|Olesko|1991|p=59, 341}} In this institution, [[Otto Hesse]] and [[Theodor Schönemann]] belonged to his students.{{sfn|Olesko|1991|p=103}}

In 1835, he was appointed —  by recommendation of [[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel]] — to the [[University of Halle]] as extraordinary professor of mathematics in succession of [[Julius Plücker]],{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|pp=32–33}} where he advanced to an [[ordinary professor]] in 1839. He worked with varied interests in analysis, mainly in the field of [[elliptic function]]s, where he made discoveries over the [[complex multiplication]],{{sfn|Cantor|1892}} further in geometry, mechanics, and history of mathematics.{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|pp=210–212}} He translated the ''History of Geometry'' by [[Michel Chasles]] (1837) into the German language,<ref>[https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/de/view/bsb10081590?page=5 ''Geschichte der Geometrie, hauptsächlich mit Bezug auf die neueren Methoden. Von Chasles. Aus dem Französischen übertragen durch Dr. L. A. Sohncke''. Gebauersche Buchhandlung, Halle 1839]</ref> and edited some of his analytic lectures. Seen as a whole, his list of publications is small;{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=210}} possible reasons could be difficult economic condition,{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=308}} since the payments for professors in Halle were low and often was not enough for their living,{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=31}} or a great burden of teaching, or a problem with alcohol.{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=308}}

Together with the physics professor Kämtz, Sohncke made an attempt in 1837 to found a seminar for mathematics and physics similar to that he had been co-founder in Königsberg, but their initiative was opposed by the biologist [[Johann Schweigger|Schweigger]]. After long negotiations, a "Seminar für Mathematik und die gesammten Naturwissenschaften" (''Seminar for Mathematics and whole Sciences'') was founded with Sohnche as head of the mathematical division; later he became director of the seminar.{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|pp=32-41}} Although it brought out considerable success, it never got the importance of the Königsberg seminar.{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=305}}

Ludwig Adolf Sohncke died in Halle on 16 January 1853; his academic successor was [[Ferdinand Joachimsthal]].{{sfn|Schlote|Schneider|2009|p=226}}
